item.text:
**6B.3 | Tinubu in 2024**
Bottom line: **mixed, leaning positive on stated prioritization and targeted programs for vulnerable groups, but weak on demonstrated outcomes and uneven on protection for children and the poorest.** The clearest positives are welfare-benefit targeting, student loans, resettlement, girls’ education, and support to conflict victims. The clearest negatives are persistent child insecurity, weak reintegration for girls, severe food insecurity, and a hard crackdown on hardship protests.

**Accepted claims**
- **President Tinubu Directs Expeditious Processing of Welfare Benefits, Demands Monthly KPI Reports** | State House | 2024-02-22 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/  
  Tinubu explicitly ordered faster delivery of welfare benefits and warned against delays harming vulnerable citizens. This is direct evidence that the administration claimed to prioritize vulnerable people in its welfare pipeline.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **With Good Governance and Commitment, We Must Overcome Old Subsidy Beneficiaries** | State House | 2024-03-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/with-good-governance-and-commitment-we-must-overcomee-old-subsidy-benificiaries-president-tinubu/  
  Tinubu tied subsidy reform to student loans, consumer credit, and social welfare, and said relief should be targeted using NIN data. That is strong intent-level evidence for prioritizing poorer households rather than treating them as an afterthought.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **In Detail: The Student Loan (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024** | State House | 2024-04-04 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/in-detail-the-student-loan-access-to-higher-education-act-2024/  
  The student-loan program was framed as an access measure for lower-income students and families. This is one of the clearest concrete pro-poor and pro-youth interventions in the 2024 record.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **President Tinubu Approves Takeoff of Consumer Credit Scheme** | State House | 2024-04-24 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-approves-takeoff-of-consumer-credit-scheme/  
  Tinubu presented consumer credit as a way to improve social mobility and help people finance housing, education, and healthcare. This supports a reading that the administration was trying to widen access for ordinary households, not just elites.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **President Tinubu Launches National Resettlement Scheme For Conflict Victims** | State House | 2024-07-06 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/  
  The administration launched a resettlement scheme for displaced and conflict-affected communities and framed it as rehabilitation and reintegration. This is the strongest direct evidence of prioritizing marginalized, conflict-affected groups.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **President Tinubu Launches Education Campaign, Sys no Child Should be Excluded from Learning** | State House | 2024-05-13 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-education-campaign-sys-no-child-should-be-excluded-from-learning/  
  Tinubu backed girls’ education, anti-GBV policy, and inclusive schooling. This is direct positive evidence for prioritizing women, girls, and children, at least in stated policy.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **President Tinubu Offers Scholarships, Housing to Families of Slain Soldiers** | State House | 2024-03-27 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-offers-scholarships-housing-to-families-of-slain-soldiers/  
  Tinubu ordered scholarships and housing support for bereaved families and pushed rapid benefit payment. This is narrow, but real, evidence of material support for vulnerable households.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms: New World Bank Financing for Inclusive Growth and Revenue Diversification** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification  
  The World Bank said the reform package aimed to create fiscal space for public services and scale up support to vulnerable households. This is external validation that the policy program was at least rhetorically and institutionally aimed at poorer groups.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **World Bank Approves New Financing for Nigeria to Improve Health Outcomes, Safety of Dams and Irrigation Services** | World Bank | 2024-09-26 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/26/world-bank-approves-new-financing-for-nigeria-to-improve-health-outcomes-safety-of-dams-and-irrigation-services  
  This package targeted health, basic education governance, and irrigation/hydropower resilience, with implied benefits for poorer and lagging communities. It is the strongest service-delivery evidence I found for the poor-region / vulnerable-group side.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- **Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk  
  HRW said authorities had failed to sustain safe-learning measures, leaving schoolchildren at continuing risk. This undercuts any claim that children were genuinely prioritized in outcomes, not just in speeches.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9

- **Nigeria: Girls Failed by Authorities After Escaping Boko Haram Captivity** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/nigeria-girls-failed-by-authorities-after-escaping-boko-haram-captivity-new-report/  
  Amnesty documented unlawful detention and weak reintegration support for girls and young women escaping Boko Haram captivity. This is strong evidence that vulnerable women and conflict survivors were not effectively prioritized in practice.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **At least 3 killed in Nigeria at protests over high cost of living** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376  
  Reuters tied the protests to inflation, subsidy removal, and cost-of-living pain, showing that poorer households were still absorbing the worst shocks. That is negative evidence on whether the state had actually prioritized them successfully.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **Insecurity, rising costs push 31 million Nigerians into acute food shortage, study says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474  
  The report said 31.8 million Nigerians were acutely food insecure. That is the clearest negative evidence that the poorest and most vulnerable were not being effectively protected from material deprivation in 2024.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/  
  Amnesty said police killed at least 24 protesters and detained more than 1,200 during protests centered on corruption and economic hardship. This suggests the administration answered vulnerable people’s grievances with coercion rather than focused protection.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.8, 3B.4

- **Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency** | BusinessDay | 2024-02-21 | https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/  
  The son-in-law appointment to the Federal Housing Authority is a concrete nepotism signal. It weakens the claim that housing and related welfare access were being allocated primarily to marginalized groups rather than insiders.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **4 Nigerian journalists charged with cybercrime, defamation over fraud investigation** | CPJ | 2024-02-09 | https://cpj.org/2024/02/4-nigerian-journalists-charged-with-cybercrime-defamation-over-fraud-investigation/  
  Charging journalists who reported on corruption weakens oversight of who captures state resources and who gets left behind. That is indirect, but it cuts against a serious prioritization of marginalized groups.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.1, 5B.7, 5B.8

- **Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting** | CPJ | 2024-10-03 | https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/  
  Continued use of cybercrime charges against journalists suggests a punitive information environment. That makes it harder to monitor whether welfare claims are reaching vulnerable groups or merely serving as rhetoric.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.1, 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **President Tinubu: I have no Cabal or Sponsors to Compensate** | State House | 2024-07-26 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-i-have-no-cabal-or-sponsors-to-compensate/  
  Tinubu denied patronage politics and highlighted ward-level social support, student loans, consumer credit, and minimum-wage increases. This is relevant counterevidence, but it remains rhetoric and does not by itself show that marginalized groups actually benefited.  
  **QIDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

**Search gap**
- I found **clear evidence for children, women/girls, conflict victims, and poor households**, but much less direct evidence for **elderly people, disabled people, and ethnic/minority communities** specifically.
- I also found **little direct 2024 evidence on water and sanitation access** targeted to marginalized groups, beyond broader infrastructure/resilience financing.
- So the best calibrated conclusion is: **Tinubu did prioritize several vulnerable categories in policy design, but 2024 outcomes still show major failures for children, girls, and the poorest, and the record is thin on elderly, disabled, and minority-specific protection.**
